goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when `embed_category` site setting is absent or doesn't match a category
Migration SQL injection or crash via unescaped host values in INSERT statement
Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update and destroy actions raise 500 instead of 404 when host record is not found
EmbeddingController#update silently discards all submitted changes and never persists parameters

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` after `before_filter :fetch_embedding` builds an `OpenStruct` from current DB state (`EmbeddableHost.all...`). It never reads `params`, never updates any model or SiteSetting, and never calls `save`, so any data submitted to `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` would be ignored while still returning a success response. This matches the finding that changes are silently discarded/not persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns `false` sentinel instead of `nil`, creating inconsistent return types for callers

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns `false` on parse/host failures (`return false unless uri.present?` / `return false unless host.present?`), but on success it returns an ActiveRecord object or `nil` (`where(...).first`). This creates a method with three possible return types (`EmbeddableHost`, `nil`, `false`) instead of the more conventional `record-or-nil`, which can trip up callers that expect `nil` for “not found/invalid” (e.g., code using `nil?`, safe navigation, or relying on ActiveRecord-like semantics).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on sites without embed_category setting because execute(...)[0] returns nil when no rows are returned, causing NoMethodError
Hot-path DB query on every embed view with no caching or index, regressing from zero DB queries to one unindexed query per embed request

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes embed access control from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` (string parsing, no DB) to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` — a DB query on every embed request. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates the table but adds no index on `host` (and the query is on `lower(host)`), so this lookup is not verifiably indexed and will likely be a full scan as the table grows. No caching is introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lower(host) = ? query cannot use a plain B-tree index, requiring a functional index or application-level cache

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` using `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, but the migration `create_embeddable_hosts` does not add any index on `host` at all. Since there is no plain B-tree index to begin with, it’s not verifiable from this diff that `lower(host)` is preventing use of an existing index; the query would be a full table scan regardless. While a performance improvement could be to add an index (possibly functional) for case-insensitive lookup, the specific finding as stated is not grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded query materializes all embeddable hosts into memory with no limit or pagination in admin embedding controller

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding`, the code sets `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`. While this does represent an unpaginated collection, the controller’s purpose (rendering the full list of allowed embeddable hosts for an admin settings screen) inherently requires returning all hosts. There is no indication in the diff of an expected limit/pagination contract, nor any introduced bug/security issue—this is a scalability concern only if the table becomes extremely large, which is speculative and not a clear defect based on the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL interpolation of host values in data migration risks broken SQL or injection from single quotes in host strings
Migration crashes on most installations due to nil dereference on `embed_category` lookup

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the code does:

```rb
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If `embed_category` is unset/blank or doesn’t match any `categories.name`, the SQL join returns zero rows. Then `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises (nil dereference) before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. This is a verifiable crash path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy` crash on missing record

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists, `host` will be `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` which immediately does `host.host = ...` and `host.category_id = ...`, causing a `NoMethodError` on `nil`. `destroy` calls `host.destroy` and will also raise on `nil`. There is no nil-check or `find`-style exception handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `before_validation` crashes on nil/blank host instead of producing a validation error
SQL injection / quote-breaking via unescaped host values in migration

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts` (split by newlines). Because `h` is not escaped/quoted via the connection (e.g., `quote(h)`), any host value containing a single-quote will break the SQL, and a maliciously crafted value could inject arbitrary SQL during migration execution. This is a verifiable quote-breaking/injection risk in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of public `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` and `SiteSetting.embed_category` without deprecation

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally replaces the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` / `SiteSetting.embed_category` configuration with a new `EmbeddableHost` model + admin UI, and it includes a migration that copies existing values into `embeddable_hosts` and then deletes the old site_settings keys. All core references to these settings are removed/updated in the diff (e.g., `EmbedController`, `TopicEmbed`, `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` is deleted). The proposed issue about “without deprecation” is more of a backward-compatibility/policy concern for external consumers/plugins, which is not verifiable as a defect from this diff alone and does not show an introduced bug in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a no-op; accepts PUT but changes nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action (wired to `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` in `config/routes.rb`) does not read any params or persist any changes; it only `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, same as `show`. So the PUT endpoint is effectively a no-op and cannot update anything server-side as implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `expandable_first_post?` no longer gates on configured embeddable hosts
Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category site setting is absent or doesn't match a category, making the fallback unreachable

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does:

```rb
category_id = execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If the `embed_category` site_setting row is missing, or if its `value` doesn’t match any `categories.name`, the JOIN returns 0 rows, so `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`. Calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, so the later fallback:

```rb
if category_id == 0
  category_id = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i
end
```

is never reached. This is a verifiable crash path introduced by the migration code as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection vulnerability via unescaped host values interpolated directly into INSERT statement in migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes from the `site_settings` table (`embeddable_hosts` value split by newlines). Because `h` is not quoted/escaped via the DB adapter (e.g., `quote`/bind params), a malicious or even just malformed value containing a `'` could break the query, and if an attacker can influence that site setting it can become SQL injection during migration execution. This is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy raise NoMethodError on missing record instead of returning 404
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same problem: in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy, a missing EmbeddableHost record can result in nil, and subsequent method calls on it cause a NoMethodError (the candidate additionally notes the desired behavior would be a 404).

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true in migration can silently destroy existing data on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. That means if this migration is ever executed against a database where `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g., partial/failed deploy, manual table creation, conflicting branch/history), it can silently destroy existing data instead of failing fast. This behavior is directly implied by `force: true` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a silent no-op that doesn't apply or persist submitted params

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not read any request params and performs no persistence or mutation; it simply re-renders the serialized `@embedding` OpenStruct (populated by `fetch_embedding` as `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). Since there is also a `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` route wired to this action, any submitted changes to “embedding” would be silently ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost before_validation callback crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the before_validation callback calls a string method (sub!) on self.host, and if host is nil it raises a NoMethodError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing uniqueness validation and DB index on embeddable_hosts.host, allowing duplicates and degrading query performance

adjudication.rationale: The new EmbeddableHost model only validates host format and does not validate uniqueness. The migration creates embeddable_hosts with columns host and category_id but adds no unique constraint/index on host. Lookups use `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `record_for_host`, so duplicate rows for the same host are possible and would make behavior ambiguous (which category applies depends on which row happens to be returned) and can also hurt performance since host checks are used in request paths (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs for EmbeddableHostsController and EmbeddingController only assert inheritance, leaving CRUD logic, validation, error rendering, and destroy actions untested

adjudication.rationale: The new specs at `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each contain only one example asserting the controller subclasses `Admin::AdminController`. They do not exercise any of the actual controller behavior added in the diff (e.g., `create/update/destroy` in `EmbeddableHostsController`, parameter handling, failure paths via `render_json_error`, or `EmbeddingController#show/#update` serialization). This is directly verifiable from the diff and represents insufficient test coverage for the newly introduced CRUD logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is effectively a no-op—it re-renders but never persists changes, which is a likely bug

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` only `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads params or persists anything. `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`, so there is nothing to save, and PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` will always be a no-op success response. This is reinforced by the client controller `admin-embedding.js.es6` having a `saveChanges` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit this no-op endpoint and misleadingly appear to “save” changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for invalid host format validation in embeddable_host_spec.rb—no test asserts that invalid or malformed hosts fail validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `validates_format_of :host` in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, and `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` only tests normalization (trimming http/https/paths) and `host_allowed?` behavior; it does not include any example asserting that an invalid/malformed host is rejected as invalid. However, this is a test coverage gap rather than a functional bug/correctness defect in the implementation itself, so it’s not a “real” code problem introduced by the diff under the stated criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in expandable_first_post? is not properly covered—no test for the scenario where embed_truncate is true, has_topic_embed? is true, but no EmbeddableHost records exist, where the new code returns true instead of false
No JavaScript tests for the new admin embedding UI (embeddable-host component and admin-embedding controller actions)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new Ember admin UI code (adapter, route, controller, component, and Handlebars templates) but does not add any corresponding JavaScript test files. However, the absence of tests is a process/coverage concern rather than a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff; nothing in the diff is shown to be failing or incorrect solely due to missing JS tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates user-controlled host data into SQL string, risking SQL injection or breakage with hosts containing single quotes, and has no migration test

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds raw SQL with string interpolation of `h` from the existing `site_settings` value: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. If any stored host line contains a single quote (or other special characters), the SQL will break; and because it is unescaped interpolation, it also constitutes an SQL injection vector from data already in the DB (even if typically only admins can set it). The diff does not add any migration spec/test either, though lack of such a test is more of a process gap than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for host_allowed? with nil, empty string, or malformed referer input, despite explicit rescue/return guards for these cases

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`/`record_for_host` with guards for malformed input, but the absence of direct unit tests for nil/empty/malformed referer values is a test-coverage suggestion, not a verifiable defect in the code. The code already returns false safely for malformed input (`URI(host) rescue nil` + presence checks), and there is at least a malformed-URL test path in `TopicEmbed.import` ("returns nil when the URL is malformed"), even if it doesn’t assert `host_allowed?` directly. Therefore this finding does not identify a real problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes when `embed_category` site setting is absent because `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the migration assuming execute(...)[0]['id'] exists and crashing when the query returns no rows (missing embed_category setting), causing a NoMethodError/nil access. Same underlying bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection / broken INSERT risk via unescaped host values interpolated directly into raw SQL in migration

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds an INSERT using string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value (`embeddable_hosts`). This is not SQL-escaped/quoted safely. If any stored host line contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, the migration can error (broken SQL) or, in principle, allow SQL injection during migration execution. Using bound params or `quote(h)` would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files are swapped: `category_fabricator.rb` defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `Fabricator(:category)`

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and a new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `Fabricator(:category)` (and related category fabricators). However, both fabricators (`:category` and `:embeddable_host`) still exist somewhere under `spec/fabricators/`, and Fabrication typically loads fabricators by requiring all files in that directory rather than relying on filename-to-fabricator matching. So this is a confusing organization change, but not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a no-op / dead code that only re-renders and never mutates anything

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` exactly like `#show` and never reads `params` or persists any changes. The route explicitly exposes `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, and the client controller includes an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit this endpoint but accomplish nothing beyond re-rendering. Even if other changes are saved via `EmbeddableHostsController`, this `update` action is effectively a no-op as implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHostSerializer` redefines attributes as explicit no-op methods that do exactly what the serializer would do by default

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHostSerializer` declares `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` and then defines instance methods `id`, `host`, and `category_id` that simply return `object.id`, `object.host`, and `object.category_id`. That is redundant, but it does not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect—ActiveModel::Serializer-style serializers would already serialize those fields by default (or equivalently via the `attributes` declaration) without the explicit no-op methods. This is a style/cleanup nit rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHost` model `record_for_host` returns `false` instead of `nil` for "not found", creating a leaky type boundary

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns `nil` when the host is well-formed but no record exists (`where(...).first`). It returns `false` only for invalid/malformed input cases (URI parse failure or missing host). So the proposed finding (“returns false instead of nil for not found”) is not verifiably true from the code, and current call sites (`present?` and `try`) handle `false` safely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored host casing is not normalized; uniqueness relies on query-time `lower()`, allowing duplicate rows with different casing

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model strips scheme/path in `before_validation` but never normalizes casing (no `downcase!`). The host format validation is case-insensitive (`/i`), and the DB migration creates `embeddable_hosts.host` without a unique index or uniqueness validation. Yet lookup uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which will treat differently-cased rows as equivalent at query time, meaning you can insert duplicate allowed hosts that differ only by case (e.g., `Example.com` and `example.com`). This is a real data-integrity/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `topic.expandable_first_post?` silently dropped the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` precondition

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (it changes from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). However, this coincides with the removal of the `embeddable_hosts` site setting entirely (deleted from `site_settings.yml`, locale, and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`), replaced by the `EmbeddableHost` model/table. Given that `expandable_first_post?` already requires `has_topic_embed?`, gating it on the old setting is no longer meaningful, and the diff does not show any clear correctness/security regression caused by dropping that condition (it may even be desirable for existing embedded topics). So the finding is an observation, not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `_focusOnInput` decorator stack couples lifecycle and observer methods, firing on every `editing` change including initial render

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `_focusOnInput` is explicitly decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`, so it will run on insert and whenever `editing` changes. However, that behavior is verifiable but not clearly a defect: focusing when entering edit mode is likely intended, and when `editing` is false the selector `.host-name` won’t match anything so `.focus()` is effectively a no-op. The finding reads more like a design/style critique than a real bug or correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes when `embed_category` site setting is absent or doesn't match a category name because `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and raises `NoMethodError`, making the fallback unreachable and the migration non-idempotent

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does:

```rb
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If there is no `embed_category` row in `site_settings`, or if it exists but `s.value` doesn’t match any `categories.name`, the query returns zero rows, so `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`. Calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, so the subsequent fallback (`if category_id == 0 ...`) is never reached. This is a concrete crash path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `create_table ... force: true` is destructive DDL with no rollback path, silently dropping an existing `embeddable_hosts` table and its data; combined with irreversible data backfill/deletes in a single `change` method, `db:rollback` would fail

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the table is created with `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists (destructive). Additionally, the migration is written as a single `change` method but includes multiple raw `execute` calls that insert data and delete rows from `site_settings` (`DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN (...)`). Raw `execute` statements are not automatically reversible, so a `db:rollback` would be treated as irreversible (or at minimum would not restore deleted/modified data), making the finding valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Irreversible deletion of `embeddable_hosts` / `embed_category` site settings runs unconditionally even when backfill failed to insert rows, destroying admin config with no recovery
SQL injection / quoting bug in backfill INSERT because `h` is interpolated raw from a site setting value without parameterization or escaping
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: raw string interpolation of `h` into an SQL statement without parameterization/escaping, creating an SQL injection/quoting vulnerability. This matches the golden comment’s concern and suggested mitigation (parameter binding/proper quoting).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill does not normalize host values (e.g. retains scheme/path), leading to mismatch with `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` which queries against normalized `URI(...).host`, silently breaking embedding until re-saved via UI
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that the migration/backfill inserts embeddable host values via raw SQL without applying the model’s normalization, so existing values containing scheme/path won’t match later lookups that compare against the normalized bare host (e.g., URI.host), causing embedding to break until normalized/re-saved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy` crash on missing record because there is no `find`/nil check, yielding a 500 instead of a 404 for stale/missing ids

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists, `host` will be `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)`, which immediately does `host.host = ...` and `host.category_id = ...`, raising `NoMethodError` on `nil`. `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on `nil`, also raising `NoMethodError`. Both cases would produce a 500 for stale/missing ids instead of a handled 404/not_found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddingController#update` ignores submitted params and renders the same object without applying any, making it dead/misleading code that silently does nothing

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads `params` or persists any changes. Since routes include `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` and the Ember controller has an action calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, this PUT endpoint is effectively a no-op that will return success without applying submitted data, which is misleading/dead behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` check changes behavior for sites with no hosts configured, breaking embedding with no error surfaced and causing unexpected `expandable_first_post?` behavior flips tied to the fragile migration

adjudication.rationale:
The diff removes the explicit `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` guard, but embedding is still blocked when no hosts are configured because `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` will return false (no DB records => `record_for_host` returns nil), and `ensure_embeddable` still raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` (“invalid referer host”). So there is no “no error surfaced” silent break; it’s largely just a different error message/path.

`Topic#expandable_first_post?` does change by dropping the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` condition, but that setting is removed in this change and embeds already imply `has_topic_embed?` is true; the diff doesn’t show a correctness defect from that flip (it may be intentional to decouple from the removed setting). The claim about a “fragile migration” causing these behavior flips is not a concrete, verifiable problem in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError if no `embed_category` row exists in `site_settings` because `result[0]` is `nil`.

adjudication.rationale:
In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does:

```ruby
category_id = execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If there is no `site_settings` row for `embed_category` (common when the setting was never explicitly set, since `site_settings` typically only stores overrides), `execute(...)` returns an empty result, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. There’s no guard before indexing into `[0]`, so the proposed crash is a real, directly verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration assumes `embed_category` stores a category name instead of a numeric ID, causing the INNER JOIN to fail and crash.
`cmd_tuples` returns 0 for SELECT statements in some `pg` gem versions, causing the host data migration to be silently skipped and resulting in data loss.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration, `embeddable_hosts = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")` returns a result set and the code gates on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` before reading `embeddable_hosts[0]['value']`. For PostgreSQL/pg (as used by ActiveRecord), `cmd_tuples` on a SELECT result reflects the number of rows returned, so this condition correctly detects whether the setting row exists. The proposed finding depends on a specific, unshown incompatibility (“some pg gem versions return 0 for SELECT”) and isn’t verifiable from the diff; the code itself does not obviously introduce the claimed silent-skip/data-loss behavior in normal supported environments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `before_validation` crashes with NoMethodError if the `host` field is `nil`, causing a 500 server error instead of a 422 validation error.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` missing/blank in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`), `sub!` will raise `NoMethodError` before validations run, resulting in a 500 instead of a normal validation error response (422/JSON error). The diff does not guard against `nil` in the callback (e.g., `return if host.blank?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection vulnerability via unescaped `h` value interpolated directly into the SQL string in the migration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` comes from `site_settings.value` (`embeddable_hosts`) and is not escaped/quoted via the DB adapter. If `h` contains a single quote or SQL (e.g. `evil.com'); DROP TABLE ...; --`), the SQL becomes syntactically altered, which can at minimum break the migration and can enable SQL injection in the context of the migration run. The diff shows no sanitization/quoting before interpolation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing `.catch()` handler on `destroyRecord()` promise, causing silent failures and no UI feedback when a DELETE request fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` with no `.catch(...)` handler. If the DELETE request fails (network/server/permission), the promise rejection is not handled here and no UI error handler like `popupAjaxError` (used in `save()`) is invoked, so the user won’t get explicit feedback from this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Port mismatch where `before_validation` preserves ports in the host string, but `record_for_host` strips the port via `uri.host`, causing the query to never match the stored host.

adjudication.rationale: Real mismatch: `EmbeddableHost` can persist a host including a port (validation regex allows `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and `before_validation` only strips scheme and path, not `:port`). But `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and uses `uri.host`, which excludes the port, then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. So a stored record like `example.com:3000` will never match a referer/url like `http://example.com:3000/...` because the lookup becomes `example.com` vs stored `example.com:3000`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a silent no-op that ignores request params and re-serializes current state, causing settings to not persist.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the current `@embedding` (`render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`) and does not read or apply any request params, nor does it update any persisted state. The corresponding Ember controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding`, but the server-side `update` endpoint is a no-op. So if anything is expected to be saved via that endpoint, it will not persist.
